description:
Spec: draft-atwood-jmap-chat-00 §Chat.slowModeSeconds + commit de60acb ("soften slow-mode exemption to SHOULD with rationale").

Spec text: "slowModeSeconds is a per-Chat throttle on message rate. SHOULD exempt members holding manage_channels permission. Servers MAY define additional exempt principals. When throttled, server returns rateLimited SetError with serverRetryAfter (RFC 8620 §5.3 + the convention from this draft) indicating when the sender may retry."

Current state: Chat.slow_mode_seconds is a stored field. handle_message_set in chat-server/src/message.rs does NOT consult it on send. No rate-tracking state exists in MemoryBackend.

## Acceptance

- New ChatBackend method:
  ```rust
  fn slow_mode_check(
      &self,
      _caller: &Self::CallerCtx,
      _account_id: &Id,
      _chat_id: &Id,
  ) -> impl Future<Output = Result<(), SlowModeError>> + Send {
      async { Ok(()) }
  }
  ```
  where SlowModeError is a tiny struct/enum in chat-server::backend:
  ```rust
  pub struct SlowModeError {
      pub retry_after: jmap_types::UTCDate,
  }
  ```
- handle_message_set on create path: invokes slow_mode_check(caller, account_id, chat_id). On Err: SetError of type `rateLimited` with `serverRetryAfter` extra-field set to the returned UTCDate. (Existing chat-client crate already has a server_retry_after(&SetError) helper that reads this back.)
- MemoryBackend implements slow_mode_check as ALWAYS Ok(()). Rustdoc explicitly says "demonstration-only MemoryBackend has no rate-tracker; production backends plug in their own. The kit defines the hook; the consumer enforces."
- Test: MemoryBackend + send → always succeeds (verifies no-op default)
- Test (uses test-only TrackingBackend that returns SlowModeError with retry_after = now + 30s): Message/set create returns SetError type rateLimited with serverRetryAfter set correctly

## Out of scope

- Implementing an actual rate tracker in MemoryBackend (consumer's job, explicitly per workspace AGENTS.md)
- Per-permission SHOULD-exempt behavior in MemoryBackend (consumer's policy)
- Modifying Chat.slow_mode_seconds storage (already exists)
title: Layer B: ChatBackend::slow_mode_check + Message/set handler integration
